newsitem.title: USA: Some 60,000 New Englanders remain without power. [CORRECTED 16:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Some 60,000 New Englanders remain without power. [CORRECTED 16:35 GMT]

text.p: Some 60,000 (corrects from 50,000) New England utility customers remained without power Tuesday, three days after a storm that dumped up to 18 inches of heavy, wet snow struck the region causing trees to topple onto power lines.
Northeast Utilities said that as of Tuesday morning, 26,400 Connecticut customers were without power, as were 22,000 in New Hampshire and 2,800 in west Massachusetts.

"We're hoping to get 99 percent of those in Connecticut back by midnight to night and most of those in western Mass and New Hampshire back by 1800 EST (2300 GMT) on Wednesday," said Northeast spokeswoman Susan Millerick.
"But there are some areas of New Hampshire where there was total devastation and there it looks like Thursday or beyond" before power can be returned, she said.
MassElectric, a subsidiary of New England Electric Service, reported some 11,000 customers, mostly in central and western Massachusetts were also without power as were 1,000 in New Hampshire.
MassElectric spokeswoman Jackie Barry said some 650 crews -- some from Ontario, Canada, New York, Pennsylvania and New Jersey -- were working to restore power.
"We hope to have the majority back on line by late today," she said early Tuesday. "But because of the widespread outtages, it may take longer in some areas.
